summary: Backend testing complete for Cargo One logistics marketplace. All 36 pytest cases pass (100%). Covered auth (register customer/driver/duplicate, admin login seed, /auth/me, invalid tokens), admin (stats RBAC, list/approve/suspend drivers), jobs (create fixed & bidding, distance & suggested_price computed, /jobs/mine, /jobs/nearby driver-only with address privacy hidden and sorted by distance, accept-fixed, cannot accept bidding via /accept), bids (submit, list, accept, assigns driver + rejects others), bookings (create with 10% deposit, idempotent, /deposit creates Stripe session, /payments/status returns unpaid for uncompleted session, 404 for bogus session, /bookings/mine hides other_party & full addresses pre-payment, /messages blocked pre-payment), post-payment features simulated by DB flip: booking reveals pickup/dropoff addresses + other_party, chat send/list works, tracking POST/GET (driver only + trail), booking status transitions (travelling->delivered), POD upload+GET, review creation after POD updates driver rating. Suspended driver login returns 403.

minor.issue: success_url is hardcoded to preview URL (https://cargo-one-preview.preview.emergentagent.com) as default when origin_url not sent - fine for MVP but should be env-driven.
Auth required but no ownership/role check; any authenticated user with a session_id can query status. Consider restricting to the booking's customer.
Both driver and customer can advance status through any valid transition with no state-machine enforcement (e.g. customer could mark 'collected'). Acceptable for MVP but risky.
No duplicate-review guard; same reviewer can post multiple reviews for the same booking and each recomputes target rating.

action_items: Consider adding ownership check to GET /api/payments/status/{session_id}.
Consider strict booking status state-machine (only driver can advance to travelling/collected/delivered; only customer can complete).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1062 lines - consider splitting into routers (auth.py, jobs.py, bookings.py, admin.py) for maintainability (>700 line guideline).
MongoDB _id correctly excluded everywhere via projections or filter comprehensions.
Passwords hashed with bcrypt via passlib; JWT via PyJWT with configurable secret/algorithm - good.
Privacy rules (public_job include_private) correctly gate pickup_address/dropoff_address for /jobs/nearby, /bookings/mine (pre-paid), and reveal after payment_status=paid - verified in tests.
Deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup') / ('shutdown') should be migrated to lifespan context manager (FastAPI >=0.93).
STRIPE_API_KEY read at module load; if key missing app fails to import - fine for enforced fail-fast policy.
seed_data_creation: Test users created with test_*_@example.com pattern (customers, drivers) and a throwaway suspended driver. Test jobs prefixed with 'TEST '. Deposit test may create a Stripe test checkout session (mock/test key).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full pytest regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_cargoone_api.py runs end-to-end in ~7s and simulates deposit payment by direct Mongo flip (pymongo required) to test post-payment features without a real Stripe checkout. Uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL / preview URL. Admin seeded by backend startup (admin@cargoone.com / admin123). Note pydantic EmailStr rejects .test TLD; use @example.com in fixtures.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no failing production behavior. Two test-side issues encountered and fixed during authoring: (1) pydantic email validator rejects reserved '.test' TLD - changed fixture domain to example.com; (2) autouse _force_paid fixture was clobbering booking.status back to deposit_paid before review test - fixed to only advance status if still in pending/accepted.
